name: git_add
description: Add file contents to the index (git add <pathspec>).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git add in

arguments.name: files
arguments.desc: Optional array of files to add. If omitted, all files are added.

name: git_blame
description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file (git blame <file>).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git blame in

arguments.name: file
arguments.desc: The file to blame

name: git_branch
description: List or create branches (git branch).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: Git branch action to be executed

arguments.name: branch_name
arguments.desc: (Optional) Name of the branch to create or delete

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git branch in

name: git_checkout
description: Switch branches or restore working tree files (git checkout <branch>).

arguments.name: branch
arguments.desc: The branch to checkout. This must be a valid branch name without spaces

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git checkout in

name: git_commit
description: Record changes to the repository (git commit -m <message> [files...]).

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Optional commit description/body

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git commit in

arguments.name: files
arguments.desc: Optional array of files to commit. If omitted, all staged changes are committed.

arguments.name: message
arguments.desc: The commit message

name: git_commit_composer
description: Show the commit composer for a repository, will open a UI if client supports it.

arguments.name: custom_instructions
arguments.desc: Free-form guidance for the AI commit composer. Only meaningful when 'direction' is 'custom'.

arguments.name: direction
arguments.desc: Initial grouping preset for the composer. 'auto' lets the AI choose; 'area' groups by codebase area / subsystem; 'type' groups by conventional commit type; 'custom' uses the supplied 'custom_instructions' text. Defaults to 'auto'.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: git_fetch
description: Download objects and refs from another repository (git fetch).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git fetch in

name: git_graph
description: Show the commit graph for a repository (git log --graph), will open a UI if client supports it.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: git_log_or_diff
description: Show commit logs or changes between commits (git log --oneline or git diff).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: The action to perform: 'log' for commit logs or 'diff' for changes

arguments.name: authors
arguments.desc: Optional array of author names or emails to filter commits by (only applies to 'log' action)

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run the command in

arguments.name: revision_range
arguments.desc: Optional revision range (e.g., 'HEAD', 'main..feature', 'abc123', 'HEAD~5..HEAD'). For 'diff' action, shows differences for the specified range. For 'log' action, shows commits in the range. Defaults to HEAD.

arguments.name: since
arguments.desc: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits after (e.g., '2024-01-01', '2 weeks ago', 'yesterday', '1 hour ago', '3 days ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

arguments.name: until
arguments.desc: Optional date/timestamp/relative time to show commits before (e.g., '2024-12-31', '1 week ago', 'today', 'yesterday', '2 hours ago'). Only applies to 'log' action.

name: git_pull
description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch (git pull).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git pull in

name: git_push
description: Update remote refs along with associated objects (git push).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git push in

name: git_resolve
description: Show the conflict resolution UI for a repository, will open a UI if client supports it.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: Optional guidance for the AI conflict resolution flow.

name: git_stash
description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory (git stash).

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git stash in

arguments.name: include_untracked
arguments.desc: When true, include untracked files in the stash.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Optional name for the stash (used as the stash message)

arguments.name: staged_only
arguments.desc: When true, stash only the currently staged changes and leave unstaged work untouched.

name: git_status
description: Show the working tree status (git status), will open a UI if client supports it.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: git_worktree
description: List or add git worktrees (git worktree <action>).

arguments.name: action
arguments.desc: Git worktree action to be executed

arguments.name: branch
arguments.desc: (Optional) Existing branch for the new worktree (used for add)

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: The directory to run git worktree in

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: (Optional) Path for the worktree (required for add)

name: gitkraken_workspace_list
description: Lists all Gitkraken workspaces

name: gitlens_launchpad
description: Gitlens Launchpad. Gets your open pull requests prioritized by what needs attention: ready to merge, has conflicts, awaiting review, etc. Helpful for checking todos, outstanding tasks, or deciding what to work on next.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

name: gitlens_start_review
description: Gitlens Start Review. Creates a dedicated worktree and reviews your PR with an AI agent.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the review focus, review criteria, or what aspects to check. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions. Examples: 'focus on security issues', 'check for performance regressions', 'review only the authentication logic'.

arguments.name: pr_url
arguments.desc: URL of the PR to start review.

name: gitlens_start_work
description: Gitlens Start Work. Creates a work based on an issue. This tool will create a branch and link it with the issue, keeping context visible throughout your work.

arguments.name: directory
arguments.desc: Path of the working directory.

arguments.name: instructions
arguments.desc: OPTIONAL. Use this ONLY if the user explicitly provided specific requirements about the implementation approach, or additional context to supplement the issue. Do NOT use this parameter unless you are 100% certain about the user's intentions.

arguments.name: issue_url
arguments.desc: URL of the issue to start work on.

name: issues_add_comment
description: Add a comment to an issue

arguments.name: azure_organization
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: azure_project
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: comment
arguments.desc: The text content of the comment

arguments.name: issue_id
arguments.desc: The ID of the issue to comment on

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: Specify the issue provider

arguments.name: repository_name
arguments.desc: Repository name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

arguments.name: repository_organization
arguments.desc: Organization name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

name: issues_assigned_to_me
description: Fetch issues assigned to the user. Set assigned_to_me=false to broaden the result to all visible issues. To filter server-side by assignee, set unassigned=true for issues with no assignee, or assigned_to=<user> for issues assigned to a specific person (assigned_to_me, unassigned and assigned_to are mutually exclusive). Narrow results further with repository_name/repository_organization (GitHub), project/issue_type (Jira), or is_closed.

arguments.name: assigned_to
arguments.desc: List only issues assigned to this user (username/email/accountId, provider-dependent). Mutually exclusive with assigned_to_me and unassigned. Not supported by Trello/Linear.

arguments.name: assigned_to_me
arguments.desc: Whether to limit results to issues assigned to you. Defaults to true.

arguments.name: azure_organization
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: azure_project
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: fields
arguments.desc: Optional comma-separated list of top-level fields to keep on each result. Recommended for list/overview calls: omitting it returns every field, which on large lists can overflow the context window. Omit only when you need the full objects. Available fields: id, url, number, provider, repoName, repoOwner, repoHost, project, title, description, issueType, status, updatedAt, assignees, comments, childIssues.

arguments.name: is_closed
arguments.desc: Set to true to return closed/done issues instead of open issues. Defaults to false.

arguments.name: issue_type
arguments.desc: Issue type. Jira only (e.g. Bug, Story, Task).

arguments.name: page
arguments.desc: Optional parameter to specify the page number, defaults to 1

arguments.name: project
arguments.desc: Project key. Jira only (e.g. GKDEV).

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: Specify the issue provider

arguments.name: repository_name
arguments.desc: Repository name. GitHub only; must be combined with repository_organization.

arguments.name: repository_organization
arguments.desc: Organization name. GitHub only.

arguments.name: unassigned
arguments.desc: Set to true to list only unassigned issues. Mutually exclusive with assigned_to_me and assigned_to. Not supported by Trello.

name: issues_create
description: Create a new issue. For Jira, repository_name is the project key. For Linear, repository_organization is the team UUID, key, or name.

arguments.name: assignees
arguments.desc: Optional list of assignees. GitHub: usernames; GitLab: user IDs; Jira/Linear/Azure: first entry is used

arguments.name: azure_organization
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: azure_project
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: body
arguments.desc: The body/description of the issue (markdown supported where the provider allows)

arguments.name: issue_type
arguments.desc: Issue type. Jira only (e.g. Bug, Story, Task); defaults to Task.

arguments.name: labels
arguments.desc: Optional list of label names to apply

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: Specify the issue provider

arguments.name: repository_name
arguments.desc: Repository name. Required for GitHub/GitLab; required for Jira, where it is the project key (e.g. GKCLI)

arguments.name: repository_organization
arguments.desc: Organization name. Required for GitHub/GitLab; for Linear use as team identifier

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: The title of the issue

name: issues_get_detail
description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific issue by its unique ID. For Jira Epics, the response includes a childIssues array containing all issues linked to the epic.

arguments.name: azure_organization
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps organization name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: azure_project
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: issue_id
arguments.desc: The Number or ID of the issue to retrieve. Supported formats include GitHub/GitLab numeric IDs (e.g., 123 or #123), Jira keys (e.g., PROJ-123), Linear issue IDs (UUID format), etc.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: Specify the issue provider

arguments.name: repository_name
arguments.desc: Repository name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

arguments.name: repository_organization
arguments.desc: Organization name. This is required for GitHub and GitLab

name: pull_request_assigned_to_me
description: Search pull requests where you are the author or assignee. Set reviewer to true to also include pull requests where you are a requested reviewer (github and gitlab only).

arguments.name: azure_project
arguments.desc: Optionally set the Azure DevOps project name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps

arguments.name: fields
arguments.desc: Optional comma-separated list of top-level fields to keep on each result. Recommended for list/overview calls: omitting it returns every field, which on large lists can overflow the context window. Omit only when you need the full objects. Available fields: timestampCreatedAt, updatedAt, mergedAt, closedAt, title, description, url, state, owner, repoName, repoHost, provider, id, nodeId, repositoryId, projectId, organization, files, clone, number, merged, draft, approved, authoredByMe, headBranch, baseBranch, headRepo, author, assignees, reviews, reviewDecision, mergeableState, buildStatuses, baseRef, headRef, additions, deletions, currentViewer.

arguments.name: is_closed
arguments.desc: Set to true if you want to search for closed pull requests

arguments.name: page
arguments.desc: Optional parameter to specify the page number, defaults to 1

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: Specify the git provider

arguments.name: repository_name
arguments.desc: Set the repository name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

arguments.name: repository_organization
arguments.desc: Set the organization name of the pull request. Required for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket

arguments.name: reviewer
arguments.desc: Set to true to also include pull requests where you are a requested reviewer. Supported by github, github_enterprise, gitlab, gitlab_self_hosted; ignored for Azure DevOps and Bitbucket.

arguments.name: with_branches
